units.name: U01-1 Orange Marilyn
units.passage: Andy Warhol created "Orange Marilyn," a silkscreen piece that measures 20 by 16 inches, after the death of Marilyn Monroe in 1962. Works of this kind begin as a photograph. Next, the artist puts colors on top of it so that the mood of the photo changes. Some people believe Warhol wanted to say something about fame: in modern society, a star seems less like a person and more like a product. Of Warhol's many silkscreens of Monroe, "Orange Marilyn" is the best known because of its amazing rise in price. At first, the work was not expensive. Leo Castelli bought it for only $250. Years later, in 1998, after Warhol's death, it came up for auction and was bought for $17.3 million. That is over 10,000 times what Castelli had paid. Over the years, buyers have paid more for Warhol's art than for Picasso's. What makes his work so valuable? One reason is that people understand it easily. The head of the Andy Warhol Museum puts it this way: "Hang a Jackson Pollock on your wall, and not many of your friends will recognize it. With a Warhol, there is nothing you need to explain."

units.name: U01-2 The Life of Andy Warhol
units.passage: Andy Warhol was born in Pittsburgh in 1928. His parents were immigrants from Slovakia. Even as a young child, he was good at drawing and painting. He went to the Carnegie Institute of Technology, where he majored in commercial art. When he finished school, he moved to New York. There, he drew pictures for magazines and commercial advertising, and he soon made a name for himself as an illustrator. During the 1960s, Warhol began to paint everyday objects, like Campbell Soup cans and bottles of Coke. One of his friends gave him this idea. The friend told Warhol to paint the things that Warhol himself loved most. Warhol loved celebrities too, so they also became his subjects. He created silkscreen prints of stars such as Marilyn Monroe and Elizabeth Taylor. He set up a studio named The Factory in 1962. There he employed "art workers," and together they mass-produced his silkscreen prints in many different versions. People called Warhol "the Prince of Pop Art," a title he achieved through hard work. He elevated ordinary objects of daily life to the status of art. In addition, he erased the line separating fine art from commercial art.

items.exp: 워홀의 출생과 교육, 삽화가 시절, 팝아트 활동과 업적을 순서대로 소개하고 있어요.

units.name: U02-1 Animals and Memory
units.passage: People and dogs remember things in very different ways. Imagine meeting an old friend again. You can recall the place and the time of your last meeting, and perhaps even the clothes you had on. That is, you remember an event. According to recent research, dogs and other animals are unable to do this. In fact, many animals seem to have very poor short-term memories. A dog may forget an event just two minutes after it happens! From dolphins to bees, many animals have memories that last only seconds. You might object, "What about the old saying 'an elephant never forgets'? Can't some animals remember things for a long time?" That is partly true. Animals keep the memories that help them survive. Some birds, for example, remember the spots where they stored their food. Animals also link memories with feelings. Your dog knows you are a good person; however, it cannot recall when or where it last saw you. Why does this difference matter? Remembering events allows humans to create history. In our minds, we can 'time travel' back to the past. Are animals able to do the same? We don't think so.

units.name: U02-2 Do You Have a Good Memory?
units.passage: Of all the work the human brain does, remembering information is among the most complex processes. Memory comes in three types: sensory memory, short-term memory, and long-term memory. Sensory memory copies exactly what our eyes see or our ears hear. Next, the brain judges whether this information matters enough to keep. Important information is passed on to either short-term memory or long-term memory, while unimportant information is quickly forgotten. Sensory memory lasts for less than one second. Short-term memory is able to hold about 7 items, give or take 2. Its duration is usually just a few seconds. Without it, we could not work on problems. When we write an essay, for instance, we have to remember the sentence we just finished while writing the next one. Long-term memory works like an enormous web of data that stores everything we have remembered. Information moves from short-term to long-term memory when we repeat it or link it to things we already know. Some people think sleep plays an important role in building long-term memory. In their view, short-term memories change into long-term ones more effectively while we sleep.

units.name: U03-1 More Visitors to Machu Picchu?
units.passage: REPORTER: In Peru, some people would like more and more tourists to come to Machu Picchu, but others disagree. What is your opinion about more visitors coming to this historic site? ADELMO: My home is close to Machu Picchu. I believe Peru needs to make more effort to bring tourists here. Visitors spend money, which makes the local economy stronger, and that means more jobs for us. In addition, international tourists and local people get a chance to learn about one another's cultures. Lastly, people will realize how important it is to take good care of Machu Picchu. Then it will remain beautiful for many years. BEATRIZ: In my opinion, Peru should limit how many tourists can visit Machu Picchu each year. There are already too many visitors, and this causes serious problems. To begin with, crowds of tourists can be bad for the old ruins. Little by little, visitors damage them, and a few people even move or break the ancient stones. Also, some tourists harm the environment by leaving trash everywhere. If the number of visitors keeps growing, Machu Picchu could easily become an ugly place.

units.name: U03-2 An Ancient City of Mysteries
units.passage: High in the Andes Mountains stands Machu Picchu, an ancient city built in about 1450. Many call it one of the loveliest and most mysterious places on Earth. After the Spanish destroyed the Inca civilization, the city was forgotten. The outside world learned about it only in 1911, when Hiram Bingham, an American historian, found it. The city contains hundreds of stone structures, such as palaces, temples, parks, fountains, and homes. Many of its buildings were made without any mortar. Instead, the builders cut blocks of stone so that they fit together perfectly. According to some people, the fit is so perfect that you cannot even slide a knife blade into the gaps. Quite a few of the blocks weigh as much as 50 tons or more. Nobody knows for sure how the people moved and placed such enormous stones. After all, the builders had neither horses nor wheels! Today, Machu Picchu draws visitors from around the globe. As more and more tourists arrive, however, the danger to the city is growing. It now appears among the 100 Most Endangered Sites.

units.name: U04-1 Living with Etna
units.passage: Rising more than 3,327 meters, Mount Etna is the highest active volcano in Europe. Its loud noises, smoke, and gas remind people that the volcano is alive. An eruption could happen at any time. Despite these dangers, many people have formed a strong bond with Etna. The mountain stands on Sicily's eastern coast in Italy, and people have lived around it for centuries. Even today, thousands of people live and farm there. The soil, enriched by volcanic ash, is excellent for farming, so the farmers grow various crops. In addition, a large number of tourists travel there to view the volcano firsthand, and the local people earn money from them. It is not surprising, then, that UNESCO named Mount Etna a World Heritage site in 2013. Still, while Etna is a wonderful place to visit, living there is not easy. The town of Nicolasi lies only 19 kilometers from the crater, and it has been destroyed two times. Villages close to the crater are in danger every day. Even so, the people have not moved away. Perhaps they have learned how to live in harmony with Mount Etna.

units.name: U04-2 How Volcanoes Erupt
units.passage: If we want to know how a volcano works, we must first look at how our planet is built. The Earth is made up of three layers: the core in the middle, the mantle around it, and the crust on the outside. The core, which lies at the Earth's center, is made of solid rock. We live on the outer crust, which is solid and between 5 and 50 kilometers thick. Between the core and the crust is the mantle, the largest of the three layers. Most of the time, it stays solid. Under certain circumstances, however, material in the mantle melts and becomes a hot liquid rock called magma. The magma collects in a big underground pool. Once the pressure becomes great enough, the magma breaks through a weak spot in the crust and bursts out as lava. Hot gas, ash, and lava make volcanoes powerful and dangerous. In 2010, for example, the Eyjafjallajökull volcano in Iceland erupted, and clouds of ash covered much of Europe. Because planes could not fly, tens of thousands of travelers were stuck for days before they could return home. Farms near the volcano were also ruined by lava and ash. The eruption brought many human activities to a standstill.

units.name: U05-1 An Italian-style Coffee Shop
units.passage: Starbucks is now the largest coffee chain on Earth, running over 28,000 shops across 76 countries. But when the company began in 1971, it was just one small store in downtown Seattle. Ten years later, in 1981, Howard Schultz stopped by this little coffee bean shop. He was so impressed by its coffee and the way it did business that he became part of the company the following year. In 1983, Howard took a trip to Italy. Once there, he was surprised to find that the local coffee bars were wonderful spots where people gathered and spent time together. He hoped to bring this Italian custom back to America. When Howard later became the head of Starbucks, he made (a) his dream come true. He filled every shop with a cozy, relaxing atmosphere. Soon people came to Starbucks to meet friends, rest, read, listen to music, or even do homework and office work. Customers loved the idea, and the brand quickly grew popular both in the U.S. and overseas. Today, Starbucks also tries to act responsibly as a member of society. It serves drinks in cups made of recycled paper. It also supports the fair trade movement, adding more and more fair trade products to its menu.

Why Coffee Prices Keep Going Up

커피 바가 모두 재활용 컵을 사용했다.

Howard Schultz was disappointed by Italian coffee bars.
Customers did not like the idea of relaxing at Starbucks.

units.name: U05-2 Fair Trade Coffee
units.passage: Coffee ranks among the farm products traded most widely around the globe. Yet only a few people are aware that numerous small coffee farmers do not even make enough money to pay for growing it. Large coffee companies push growers to sell their beans cheaply, and because of this, the price of coffee on the global market has fallen. The fair trade movement offers one possible answer to this problem. It is based on the idea that farmers deserve a fair part of the profits. Companies that join the movement can receive a fair trade mark from special organizations. To earn this mark, a company must pay farmers at least $1.40 for each pound of coffee. It must also make loans to farmers and give them technical support for their farming. Because of these efforts, many farmers are now better off than before, and they can get health care and education. Fair trade has also become popular with shoppers. More and more people are concerned about how coffee farmers live and work. Coffee lovers are pleased because they know that the more cups of coffee they enjoy, the better the farmers' lives become.

세계 커피 시장에서 큰 회사들이 성공한 비결
items.exp: 커피 농부들의 어려움과 그 해결책인 공정 무역 운동의 내용과 효과를 설명하고 있어요.

units.name: U06-1 Astronauts in the ISS
units.passage: The ISS, short for the International Space Station, is a huge satellite that was built for scientific research. Astronauts from various countries go there and live on board for a few days or for as long as several months. Their days on the station are always full, and they work for twelve hours each day. The space station resembles a large home made up of many complex parts. Because the astronauts must take good care of it, much of their time goes to housework such as cleaning and maintenance. Taking out the garbage and unpacking new supplies are two important everyday tasks in space. At times, the astronauts must even leave the spacecraft to fix something outside. This work can be dangerous, since it is almost -270°C out in space and they must move while carrying heavy equipment. The astronauts also use much of their time to set up and carry out science experiments. They study the effects of weightlessness on materials, plants, and animals. Their findings may help us learn more about nature and may also bring benefits to the economy and the environment.

The Busy Daily Life of Astronauts on the ISS

우주 비행사들은 항상 1년 이상 ISS에 머문다.
우주 비행사들은 우주선 밖으로 나가는 일이 없다.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 어법상 알맞은 것은? "Taking out the garbage and ___ new supplies are two important everyday tasks in space."
items.exp: and 앞의 동명사 Taking과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 동명사 unpacking이 알맞아요.

units.name: U06-2 Staying Clean in Space
units.passage: Staying clean is not easy in space. There is very little water, so every drop is valuable. In addition, water does not run downward there; it just floats in the air. So how do astronauts keep themselves clean while living on the ISS for half a year? Their soaps and shampoos are special products that can be rinsed off without water. They must be careful with these products, or soap bubbles will drift around everywhere. After washing, they wipe themselves dry with a towel. Brushing teeth is another problem in space. Astronauts use ordinary toothbrushes and toothpaste, just like people on Earth do. But because there is no sink on the spacecraft, they must swallow their toothpaste when they finish. All the water on the ISS is used again and again. Even the sweat in dirty clothes is collected and turned into water for drinking and other uses. In other words, astronauts might be drinking each other's sweat! Does life in space still sound exciting to you? Just remember: it comes at a price.

units.name: U07-1 Louis Pasteur's Great Work
units.passage: In 1857, a serious illness spread through Paris and killed many sheep and cows. While studying the problem, Louis Pasteur noticed something interesting. Any animal that recovered from the illness never got it again. This gave him an idea: if healthy animals were injected with a mild version of the disease, they would be protected. He was right. The injected animals stayed free of the illness, and Pasteur had created a vaccine for it. In 1885, a doctor visited Pasteur with a young boy, Joseph Meister. Joseph had been attacked and bitten by a mad dog, so the doctor feared that he would develop rabies, a deadly disease. The doctor took him to Pasteur because Pasteur was working on a vaccine for rabies. Pasteur had never given the vaccine to a human before, but he chose to use it on Joseph. It was a success, and the boy lived. During his career, Pasteur used science to solve many problems of daily life. One of them was milk, which could make people sick. Pasteur found that heating milk made it safe to drink and helped it stay fresh longer. Because of his discovery, people around the world now drink safe milk every day. We call it "pasteurized milk."

units.name: U07-2 How Vaccinations Work
units.passage: We usually get shots when we are ill. However, we sometimes get them to stay healthy. These shots are known as vaccinations. Why are they necessary? A moment of pain can protect us from many diseases and may even save lives. Indeed, vaccinations are a major reason that people today live longer. Vaccines contain the bacteria and viruses that cause illnesses, and these germs are called pathogens. However, the pathogens in a vaccine are too weak to make us ill. When we receive a vaccination, these weak pathogens enter our body. They wake up the immune system, and (a) it produces antibodies. Creating these antibodies is what protects us from diseases later on. The antibodies learn how to destroy the pathogens and keep that memory. Later, if strong pathogens get into the body, the antibodies quickly help the body defeat them. Scientists have already made vaccines against measles, chicken pox, malaria, and small pox. Someday, they might develop vaccines for many more diseases. Because of vaccines, people today can enjoy longer and healthier lives.

units.name: U08-1 Groundhog Day
units.passage: Groundhog Day is a popular North American holiday. Both Americans and Canadians celebrate it on February 2. On this day, people check the weather to guess whether winter will go on for a while or spring will come early. A groundhog, which people also call a woodchuck, is a small creature that lives in a hole it digs under the ground. Groundhogs live throughout North America, and like bears, they hibernate during the winter. According to legend, the groundhog wakes up on February 2 and crawls out of its hole. On a sunny day, it sees its own shadow and becomes scared, so it hurries back into its hole and waits for spring. On a cloudy day, however, it cannot see its shadow, so it remains above the ground. For this reason, many Americans hope for clouds on February 2, because a cloudy sky means spring is coming soon! This custom of weather forecasting started with Candlemas, a European holiday that also falls on February 2. People believed that fine weather on Candlemas meant a harsh winter was still ahead. In the 18th century, German settlers carried this belief to America, and they later chose the groundhog to predict the weather for them.

units.name: U08-2 Spring Celebrations
units.passage: People everywhere have long held celebrations for spring. To ancient people, it was a season of fresh hope and new life, so they held festivals when the hard winter was over. Customs varied from place to place, but many cultures saw the egg as a sign of new life or rebirth. In ancient Egypt and Persia, people painted eggs and ate them at spring festivals. In ancient Russia, eggs were popular spring gifts. A Russian myth tells of an egg that held a source of fire from which everything was created. Many of these traditions were assimilated into the Christian holiday of Easter. Early Christians used the egg to represent Jesus Christ's resurrection, and people still paint and eat eggs at Easter today. The spring equinox is another time for celebration in many cultures. This day usually falls around March 20, and from then on, the days are longer than the nights. Japan treats it as a national holiday, and families visit the graves of their ancestors. Many towns in Mexico hold festivales de primavera, or spring festivals. Children wear flower and animal costumes and march in parades. Some people travel to Teotihuacan, an ancient city, where they dress in white, climb the Pyramid of the Sun, and perform rituals at the top.

units.name: U09-1 Who Invented the Elevator?
units.passage: Elevators today can do surprising things. At one hotel in Germany, guests ride inside a giant fish tank, since the elevator runs through a water-filled tube full of sea creatures. For a bigger thrill, visit Sky Tower in New Zealand. Its elevator has a transparent floor and reaches the top in just 40 seconds. Like most inventions, however, the earliest elevators were very simple. Primitive lifts already existed in the 3rd century BC. These were platforms moved by people, animals, or waterwheels, and they carried heavy loads such as huge stone blocks. Around the year 1000, a book described a lifting device similar to an elevator, which people used to lift a large weapon for attacking their enemies. Beginning in the mid-19th century, factories, mines, and warehouses relied on power elevators, often run by steam, to move goods. Then, in 1853, an American inventor named Elisha Otis showed the public a freight elevator that had a safety brake. The brake stopped the elevator from falling even if its supporting cable broke. Thanks to this, people began to trust elevators more. Otis later started an elevator company, and in 1861 he received a patent for a steam elevator. Electric elevators appeared several decades after that.

units.name: U09-2 Up, Up and Away
units.passage: Imagine riding in an elevator car that travels up a cable all the way into space. This may sound like science fiction, but many scientists believe we will see space elevators become real within our lifetime. A company in Japan has even announced that it plans to build one by 2050, and in 2018, elevator experiments began at the international space station. Few people realize how inefficient it is to travel by rocket. There are several reasons why rockets might not be the ideal way to reach space. For one thing, a rocket can carry just a small number of passengers or objects, and only some rockets can be used more than once. Rockets also burn huge amounts of fuel, so every trip into space is very expensive. A space elevator, on the other hand, could make trip after trip while using much less fuel. The idea behind it is simple: Earth sits at one end, a space station sits at the other, and people ride a cable between them. Does this still seem unrealistic? Remember what people once said about flying: "That's impossible! Only birds can fly!" Today, however, countless people travel by airplane every day.

items.exp: 로켓의 비효율성과 우주 엘리베이터의 장점을 비교하고, 비행기의 예를 들어 우주 엘리베이터도 현실이 될 수 있다고 말하고 있어요.

units.name: U10-1 Sharing Books with People
units.passage: Do you have books you no longer need? Here is a fun way to handle them. You can leave them in a public place so that other people may find and read them. This practice, known as "BookCrossing," was begun in the U.S. by Ron Hornbaker in 2001. He also built the website bookcrossing.com, where people can pass books on to friends and even complete strangers. By 2018, the site had nearly two million members. Joining this network is easy. Before you leave, or "release," a book, sign in to the website and record the book there. Write down when and where you will release it, and then go out and leave it in that spot. Members can check the website for books that have been released near them and then go looking for them. The person who finds a book has to enter its identification number along with information about where and when he or she picked it up. Once the book has been read, it should be released again so that someone else can read it. Why not join this group of book lovers? BookCrossing has several benefits. You can read books for free, you can share your own books with others, and you can even help save trees.

why people stopped reading paper books

choices: The writer wonders why book lovers refuse to join.

units.name: U10-2 Teens and Fantasies
units.passage: Some people think that teenagers today never read. That is not true, though. A recent survey found that nearly 43% of American teens read for fun in their free time. In other words, many teens read books that their schoolwork does not require. Novels, and fantasies in particular, are loved by teens all over the world. For example, the Chronicles of Narnia by C. S. Lewis and the Harry Potter series by J. K. Rowling are at the top of teens' lists of favorite books. These books have been translated into dozens of languages and turned into movies as well. One student says, "Newspapers and magazines don't interest me, but I couldn't live without fantasies." What makes fantasies so fascinating to teens? The genre itself appeals to them. In a fantasy, anything is possible, and the characters are cool. Many stories are inspired by mythology, so they are filled with magic and with events that could only happen in the imagination. A good fantasy, therefore, lets readers forget the stressful real world for a while and discover an exciting world of imagination. For teens who want to relax, fantasies are a perfect escape.

units.name: U11-1 Names Around the World
units.passage: Each culture has its own customs for naming babies. Take the Gullah, an African-American community, for example. There, a baby receives two names: one is official, and the other is called a basket name. Here, a basket means a cradle that holds a baby. A basket name is usually picked according to the situation in which the baby was born. For instance, a child born on a Friday might get the basket name Friday. People in the community refer to one another by their basket names, so they often do not even know each other's official names. Malaysia has another unique naming custom. Many Malays have no family name. Instead, a man puts his father's name after his own, joined by the word "bin," meaning "son of." This means that Rosli bin Suleiman is Rosli, Suleiman's son. In the same way, women use the word "bint," meaning "daughter of." Aysha bint Suleiman, then, is Suleiman's daughter Aysha. In Korea, most given names are composed of two syllables, and siblings often share one of them. For example, Kim Jeong-min and his brother Kim Jeong-su both have "jeong" in their given names, while Kim is their family name. This practice, however, is becoming less common.

units.name: U11-2 John Who?
units.passage: In Europe, until the early Middle Ages, most people lived in small farming villages. Because everyone knew their neighbors, people hardly needed last names, or surnames. However, as towns and the number of people in them grew, keeping records became tricky. Suppose a village had six men named John. How could the tax collector be sure which Johns had paid their taxes? People needed a way to tell apart those who had the same first name. Some surnames came from where people lived. "Easter" was a perfect choice for someone who lived toward the east, and a person living near the spot where people crossed a river might be called "Ford." Other surnames came from occupations. A man whose job was baking bread took the name "Baker," and a blacksmith became "Smith." Many surnames also came from personal characteristics. Someone with brown hair could be named "Brown," and a very tall person could be named "Long." "Bright" and "Smart" are other surnames of this type. Lastly, a simple way to form a surname was to attach "son" to the end of the father's name. That is how names like "Williamson," "Johnson," and "Davidson" were created.

units.name: U12-1 The Most Famous Painkiller
units.passage: For thousands of years, people have relied on aspirin to fight pain. Its story begins with Hippocrates, a doctor in ancient Greece who lived at some point between 460 BC and 377 BC. This doctor treated headaches, pains, and fevers with a powder made from the leaves and bark of the willow tree. By 1829, chemists had found that salicin, a substance in willow plants, could relieve pain. People believed that humans would never have to suffer pain again. Salicin from willow plants, however, was tough on the stomach. In 1853, Charles Frederic Gerhardt, a scientist from France, discovered a solution to this problem, but his formula was hard to make. Then in 1897, Felix Hoffmann, a German chemist, developed a more efficient method. He gave the medicine to his father, who had arthritis, and it worked. In 1899, the new compound got its familiar name, aspirin. In the beginning, aspirin came in powder form, and it was not until 1915 that the first aspirin tablets appeared. After its invention, aspirin spread around the world in the 1920s, and during the 20th century, people found many more uses for it. Today, doctors use aspirin to bring down swelling, to treat arthritis, and to ease heart problems.

units.name: U12-2 How the Placebo Effect Works
units.passage: How can we find out if a new drug really works? Usually, scientists run an experiment with two groups of people. People in one group take the new drug, and people in the other group take a placebo, which is a pill that looks identical to the new drug, but it is not real medicine. Afterward, the results from the two groups are compared to check whether the new drug is effective. Surprisingly, placebos helped about one-third of people get better. This is known as the placebo effect. Some researchers think the mind is responsible for the effect. In their view, when people trust a placebo, they feel well and eventually recover. Placebos may also produce a physical response. A recent study showed a link between the placebo effect and endorphins, which are natural painkillers produced by the brain. Placebos have been used by doctors for a very long time. In the U.S., over half of all doctors prescribe placebos, such as vitamins, on a regular basis to help their patients. However, some people argue that this practice is not ethical because doctors deceive their patients. Others, though, see nothing wrong with it, since the doctors are only trying to help their patients.

units.name: U13-1 Bring Images to Life
units.passage: Animated cartoons were born in the early 20th century, and people have loved this kind of entertainment ever since. Each year, animated films become big hits all over the world, and audiences young and old are thrilled by the excitement they offer. What most viewers do not realize is that an animated cartoon is really just a collection of "still" pictures. These pictures are played one after another in a sequence at high speed, up to 24 of them every second. When we watch them together, they seem to move. Each still picture is known as a frame. Frames are usually made in one of two ways. In the first method, pictures are drawn and then photographed. In the second, a model is built and changed a tiny bit at a time, and a special camera takes a picture of each change. Because a cartoon requires an enormous number of frames, producing a good one used to be very hard work. Today, special computer software makes it much simpler to create lifelike characters. ___, talented animators are still necessary. Computers cannot yet make artistic choices or put real passion into simple pictures.

units.name: U14-1 Home Remedy for Snoring
units.passage: Question - Sleepless: How can I stop my roommate from snoring? Jake, my roommate, is a nice guy, but his snoring is as loud as a motorbike. Every night I try to get to sleep before he does. When I can't, I spend painful hours lying awake. What can I do? Answers - Dr. Cureall: Have him sleep on his side instead of on his back. Snoring happens when the soft tissues in the throat vibrate. If he sleeps facing up, the muscles in his throat relax and the tissues fall backward. Air moving through then makes the tissues shake, creating the noise. Tball: I agree with Dr. Cureall. Sleeping on your back is what makes you snore. Here's a trick to keep your roommate from lying on his back: take a tennis ball, cut it into two halves, and attach one half to his pajama top, between his shoulders. Whenever he rolls onto his back, the ball will give him enough discomfort to make him change position. Soon he will be sleeping on his side again. Nasalstrip: Another solution is to get him to breathe through his nose. A nasal strip can help with this. It widens his nostrils so more air gets in, and he won't need to breathe through his mouth.

units.name: U14-2 Don't Clip Your Nose Hair
units.passage: Have you ever asked yourself why we have hair in our noses? It certainly isn't there for decoration or to help the companies that sell nose hair trimmers. Actually, nose hair has an important job: it helps keep us healthy. First, nose hair acts as a filter for the nasal passages. On average, a person breathes in about 10,000 liters of air a day. Along with that air, germs, fungus and dust enter your nose. Nose hair catches them and stops them from getting into your lungs and making you ill. Second, nose hair helps to maintain the humidity level inside the nasal passages. When you breathe in, it adds heat and moisture to the air, and when you breathe out, it holds on to humidity. Your respiratory system needs this humidity. If you had no nose hair, your throat would become dry and your lungs would not work properly. Long nose hair may not look nice, but you should never remove all of it. People without nose hair catch colds, suffer allergy attacks and get other infections more easily. Older people especially need to be cautious about removing nose hair, because clipped hairs often take longer to grow back for them.

코털이 없으면 감기에 더 쉽게 걸린다.
나이 든 사람은 코털이 다시 자라는 데 더 오래 걸릴 수 있다.
items.exp: 코털은 숨을 들이쉴 때 공기에 열과 습기(heat and moisture)를 더해 준다고 했어요.

items.q: "Nose hair catches [them] and stops them from getting into your lungs."에서 [them]이 가리키는 것은?
items.exp: 바로 앞 문장에서 코로 들어오는 germs, fungus and dust를 코털이 붙잡는다는 의미예요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 어법상 가장 알맞은 것은? "If you had no nose hair, your throat ___ become dry."
items.exp: 현재 사실과 반대되는 가정(가정법 과거: If+주어+과거동사, 주어+would+동사원형)이므로 would가 알맞아요.

items.q: 이 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the best way to trim nose hair
how the lungs take in oxygen
the important roles of nose hair in keeping us healthy
why older people get sick more often
items.exp: 'nose hair has an important job: it helps keep us healthy'라며 필터 역할과 습도 유지 역할을 설명하는 글이에요.

items.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
choices: Nose hair exists mainly for decoration.
Nose hair trimmer companies recommend keeping nose hair.
People without nose hair rarely get infections.
Long nose hair may not look nice, but it should not be removed completely.
Clipped nose hair grows back faster for older people.
items.exp: 'Long nose hair may not look nice, but you should never remove all of it'이라고 했어요. 코털이 없으면 감염에 더 쉽게 걸리고, 노인은 다시 자라는 데 더 오래 걸려요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Nose hair (A) ___ harmful particles from the air and keeps the nasal passages (B) ___, so removing all of it can make you sick more easily.
items.exp: 'nose hair acts as a filter'이고 'helps to maintain the humidity level'이라고 했으므로 걸러 주고(filters) 습하게(moist) 유지한다는 내용이에요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (Actually, nose hair has an important job: it helps keep us ___.)
items.exp: 이어지는 내용이 세균을 걸러 'making you ill'을 막고 호흡기에 필요한 습도를 지켜 준다는 것이므로 healthy가 알맞아요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: It certainly isn't there for decoration or to [help] the companies
Second, nose hair helps to [maintaining] the humidity level
Along with that air, germs, fungus and dust [enter] your nose
Older people especially need to [be] cautious
items.exp: help는 to부정사(또는 동사원형)를 목적어로 취하므로 'helps to maintain'이 되어야 해요. to maintaining은 틀렸어요.

units.name: U15-1 The Oldest Snack Food
units.passage: Pretzels are a favorite snack food across Europe and North America. They are baked from long rolls of dough, and their unique shape comes from twisting strips of dough into knots and loops. How was the first pretzel made? No one knows for certain, but many people believe it is the oldest snack food in history. Some scientists say a monk invented it in the early 7th century. He lived somewhere in the south of France or the north of Italy. He shaped the dough so that it looked like the crossed arms of a child saying a prayer. Then he gave these treats to children who had learned their prayers. He named the snacks "pretiola," a Latin word meaning "little reward." In Italian, people called them "brachiola," which means "little arms." Later, pretiolas spread to Germany and Austria, where they got the name pretzels. It is said that pretzels traveled to America aboard the Mayflower in 1620. These days, the pretzel market is growing, because people consider pretzels a healthy, fat-free snack.

items.q: 이 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 프레첼이 7세기 수도사에 의해 만들어졌다는 설과 독일, 오스트리아, 미국으로 퍼져 나간 과정을 설명하고 있어요.

items.q: 이 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 프레첼은 독일의 한 수도사가 처음 만들었다.
프레첼의 모양은 기도하는 어른의 손을 본뜬 것이다.
프레첼 시장은 최근 들어 점점 줄어들고 있다.
프레첼은 1620년에 Mayflower호를 타고 미국에 전해졌다고 한다.
items.exp: 글에서 프레첼이 1620년 Mayflower호로 미국에 전해졌다고(It is said that ...) 했어요.

items.q: 수도사가 붙인 이름 "pretiola"의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: pretiola는 라틴어로 'little reward(작은 보상)'라는 뜻이고, 'little arms'는 이탈리아어 brachiola의 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a thick mixture of flour and water that is baked to make bread or snacks"
items.exp: dough는 '밀가루 반죽'으로, 프레첼은 긴 반죽(long rolls of dough)을 구워 만든다고 했어요.

items.q: 다음 두 문장의 의미가 같도록 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은? "It is said that pretzels came to America on the Mayflower." = "Pretzels are said ___ to America on the Mayflower."
items.exp: said(현재)보다 came(과거)이 앞선 시점이므로 완료부정사 to have come을 써야 해요.

items.q: 이 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Bake Pretzels at Home
The Prayers of a French Monk
Pretzels: A Snack with a Long History
items.exp: 'the oldest snack food in history'라 불리는 프레첼의 기원과 전파 과정을 설명하는 글이에요.

items.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
choices: The monk gave pretzels to children who had learned their prayers.
The pretzel's shape comes from rolling dough into balls.
The monk lived in the north of France.
Pretzels got their current name in Italy.
Brachiola is a Latin word meaning little reward.
items.exp: 'he gave these treats to children who had learned their prayers'라고 했어요. 수도사는 프랑스 남부나 이탈리아 북부에 살았고, pretzels라는 이름은 독일과 오스트리아에서 얻었어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Pretzels are believed to have been (A) ___ by a monk as a reward for children and later (B) ___ to other countries, including America.
items.exp: 'a monk invented it in the early 7th century'와 'pretiolas spread to Germany and Austria', 'traveled to America'에서 확인할 수 있어요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (He shaped the dough so that it looked like the crossed arms of a child saying a ___.)
items.exp: 수도사가 'children who had learned their prayers'에게 간식을 주었다고 했으므로 기도하는 아이의 팔 모양을 본뜬 것이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: their [unique] shape comes from twisting strips of dough
many people believe it is the [oldest] snack food in history
Later, pretiolas [spread] to Germany and Austria
people consider pretzels a healthy, fat-free [snack]
Pretzels are a [forgotten] snack food across Europe and North America
items.exp: 프레첼은 유럽과 북미에서 '사랑받는(favorite)' 간식이고 시장도 성장하고 있다고 했으므로 forgotten은 문맥에 맞지 않아요.

units.name: U15-2 What Makes Bread Rise?
units.passage: How do plain ingredients such as flour, sugar, salt and eggs turn into bread full of bubbles? The answer is yeast, which makes bread soft and tasty. It is the yeast in the dough that makes it rise. Bread made without yeast would be hard and difficult to chew. Yeast is a type of fungus. It is a single-celled organism so small that you need a microscope to see it. One gram of yeast holds 20 billion yeast cells! Although it is tiny, yeast is alive, so it can grow and it can die. When it has sugar to eat and its surroundings are moist, it multiplies quickly. But it dies if it gets too cold or too hot. That is why bakers use warm water to make bread dough. Once yeast is mixed into dough, it begins eating the sugar in it. While eating, it gives off carbon dioxide and other chemicals. As a result, the dough fills with bubbles and puffs up. Then why do people knead bread dough? This also has to do with yeast. Kneading spreads the yeast cells evenly through the dough, so the whole dough rises evenly. Kneading also makes it easier for bubbles of carbon dioxide to form in the dough.

items.q: 이 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 빵이 부풀어 오르는 데 효모가 하는 역할
items.exp: 효모가 반죽 속 설탕을 먹고 이산화탄소를 내뿜어 빵을 부풀게 한다는 내용이 중심이에요.

items.q: 이 글에 따르면 효모 1그램에 들어 있는 세포의 수는?
items.exp: 글에서 효모 1그램에는 20 billion(200억) 개의 세포가 있다고 했어요.

items.q: 이 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 효모는 건조한 환경에서 설탕을 먹으며 빠르게 번식한다.
효모는 설탕을 먹으면서 이산화탄소를 만들어 낸다.
반죽을 치대면 효모 세포가 고르게 퍼진다.
items.exp: 효모는 건조한 곳이 아니라 주변이 축축할 때(its surroundings are moist) 설탕을 먹으며 빠르게 번식한다고 했어요.

items.q: 다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to increase greatly in number"
items.exp: multiply는 '크게 증가하다, 번식하다'라는 뜻으로, 효모가 빠르게 늘어난다는 문장에 쓰였어요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은? "It is a single-celled organism ___ small that you need a microscope to see it."
items.exp: '너무 ~해서 …하다'라는 뜻의 'so+형용사+that' 구문이므로 so가 알맞아요.

items.q: 이 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Fungus: A Danger in the Kitchen
Yeast: The Tiny Living Thing That Makes Bread Rise
items.exp: 'It is the yeast in the dough that makes it rise'라며 살아 있는 작은 생물인 효모가 빵을 부풀게 하는 원리를 설명하는 글이에요.

items.q: What would bread be like if it were made without yeast?
choices: It would be full of bubbles.
It would be hard and difficult to chew.
It would be soft but tasteless.
items.exp: 'Bread made without yeast would be hard and difficult to chew'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Yeast, a living single-celled fungus, feeds on (A) ___ in the dough and gives off carbon dioxide, which makes the dough (B) ___.
items.exp: 'it begins eating the sugar in it. While eating, it gives off carbon dioxide'라고 했고, 그 결과 'the dough fills with bubbles and puffs up'이라고 했어요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (Kneading spreads the yeast cells evenly through the dough, so the whole dough rises ___.)
items.exp: 효모 세포가 반죽 전체에 '고르게(evenly)' 퍼지기 때문에 반죽 전체도 고르게 부푼다는 인과 관계예요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: The answer is yeast, which [makes] bread soft and tasty
Bread [making] without yeast would be hard and difficult to chew
yeast is alive, so it can grow and it can [die]
it begins [eating] the sugar in it
you need a microscope to [see] it
items.exp: 빵은 '만들어지는' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 'Bread made without yeast'가 되어야 해요. making은 틀렸어요.

units.name: U16-1 A Beautiful Song
units.passage: Long ago, there was a king who had a daughter. The princess usually stayed in a room high up in a tower, reading books or doing embroidery. One day, while she was sitting at the window, a song came to her from a fishing boat on the river. "What a beautiful song! A man who sings like that must be young and handsome," she said. From then on, she sat by the window daily, hoping to hear the song, but it never returned. As time passed, her anticipation turned into a broken heart, and she grew pale and weak. Full of worry, the king spoke with the princess's maid. "Your Majesty, your daughter is lovesick. You have to find the young man who sang that song," the maid said, and she sang it for him. The king immediately sent his men to find the singer, and they returned days later. "We have brought a fisherman from a nearby village. He knows the song." When the king saw the fisherman, he was speechless. The man was not young, and he was not handsome at all. How could such a man marry the princess? Still, the fisherman sang the song in the princess's room. The moment she heard it, the princess jumped out of bed and got dressed. She flung the door open.

items.q: 이 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Become a Good Fisherman
A Princess Who Fell in Love with a Song
A Maid Who Wanted to Marry a Prince
items.exp: 강에서 들려온 노래에 반해 상사병에 걸린 공주와 그 노래를 부른 사람을 찾는 이야기예요.

items.q: 이 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 공주는 탑 꼭대기 방에서 주로 책을 읽거나 수를 놓았다.
왕은 공주의 방으로 직접 가서 노래를 불렀다.
공주는 노래를 다시 듣지 못해 창백하고 약해졌다.
하녀는 왕에게 그 노래를 불러 주었다.
왕의 신하들은 근처 마을에서 어부를 데려왔다.
items.exp: 공주의 방에서 노래를 부른 사람은 왕이 아니라 신하들이 데려온 어부(the fisherman)예요.

items.q: 왕이 어부를 보고 말을 잃은(speechless) 이유로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: 어부는 젊지도 않고 전혀 잘생기지도 않았기(not young, not handsome at all) 때문에 왕은 그가 공주와 결혼할 수 있을지 걱정했어요.

items.q: 다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a feeling of excitement about something that you expect to happen"
items.exp: anticipation은 '기대'라는 뜻으로, 노래를 다시 듣기를 기다리던 공주의 마음을 나타내요.

items.q: "A man who sings like that [must] be young and handsome."의 [must]와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: She must be tired after the long trip.
You must wear a helmet when you ride a bike.
We must finish the work by tomorrow.
Students must not run in the hallway.
I must go to bed early tonight.
items.exp: 본문의 must는 '~임에 틀림없다'라는 강한 추측을 나타내며, 'She must be tired'의 must도 같은 추측의 의미예요.

items.q: 이 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the search for the singer of a song that made a princess lovesick
the daily life of a princess in a tower
how a maid became a famous singer
a fisherman who wanted to marry a princess
items.exp: 노래를 듣고 상사병에 걸린 공주를 위해 왕이 'sent his men to find the singer'하는 이야기예요. 탑에서의 일상은 도입부의 일부일 뿐이에요.

items.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
choices: The princess saw the singer's face from her window.
The king's men returned the same day.
The song the princess heard came from a fishing boat on the river.
The maid told the king that the princess was simply tired.
The princess refused to listen to the fisherman's song.
items.exp: 'a song came to her from a fishing boat on the river'라고 했어요. 신하들은 며칠 뒤(days later) 돌아왔고, 하녀는 공주가 lovesick이라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

After hearing a beautiful song, the princess became (A) ___, so the king sent his men to find the singer, who turned out to be an old, (B) ___ fisherman.
items.exp: 하녀가 'your daughter is lovesick'이라 했고, 찾아온 어부는 'not young, and he was not handsome at all'이었어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [How could such a man marry the princess?]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (How could such a man marry the princess?)
choices: The king wondered how to arrange the wedding quickly.
The king was curious about the fisherman's village.
The king wanted to know how the man learned the song.
The king believed the princess would never marry anyone.
The king thought the fisherman was not fit to marry the princess.
items.exp: 어부가 'not young, and he was not handsome at all'이었기에 왕은 그런 남자가 공주와 결혼할 수는 없다고 생각한 거예요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: hoping to hear the song, but it never [returned]
she sat by the window [rarely], hoping to hear
The king [immediately] sent his men to find the singer
items.exp: 노래를 다시 듣고 싶었던 공주는 'From then on, she sat by the window daily'라고 했으므로 rarely는 문맥에 맞지 않아요.

units.name: U16-2 The Fisherman's Broken Heart
units.passage: The princess suddenly burst out laughing. Standing in front of her was not a young, handsome prince but a humble-looking fisherman. Looking away from him, she ordered, "Shut the door." After he was sent back home, the fisherman could hardly eat or sleep, for he had fallen deeply in love. He became ill, and a few days later, the villagers discovered him dead in his hut. A large crystal was sitting on his chest. "(a) It is his heart," said a wise old woman from the village. "The princess hurt him so deeply that his heart hardened to block out the pain." The villagers put (b) the crystal into the fisherman's boat and pushed (c) it out into the river. The boat drifted to the shore near the palace, and there the king discovered the crystal. He took (d) it to the palace, had a teacup made from it, and gave the cup to the princess. That evening, she filled it with tea and sat by the window. She was about to take a sip when the fisherman's face appeared in the tea, and his sweet song filled her room. She remembered how cruel she had been. "What have I done? I'm so sorry," she said, and her tears fell into the cup.

items.q: 이 글에 나타난 공주의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 처음에는 초라한 어부를 보고 비웃었지만(burst out laughing), 마지막에는 자신의 잔인함을 떠올리며 후회하고 있어요.

items.q: 이 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 어부는 집으로 돌려보내진 뒤 거의 먹지도 자지도 못했다.
마을 사람들은 오두막에서 죽은 어부를 발견했다.
공주는 찻물 위에서 어부의 얼굴을 보았다.
왕은 수정을 왕관으로 만들어 공주에게 주었다.
items.exp: 왕은 수정으로 왕관이 아니라 찻잔(a teacup)을 만들어 공주에게 주었어요.

items.q: 글의 (a)~(d) 중 가리키는 대상이 나머지 셋과 다른 것은?
items.exp: (a), (b), (d)는 모두 어부의 가슴 위에 있던 수정을 가리키지만, (c)는 마을 사람들이 강으로 밀어 보낸 어부의 배를 가리켜요.

items.q: "the fisherman could [hardly] eat or sleep"에서 [hardly]의 뜻으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: hardly는 '거의 ~않다'라는 부정의 뜻으로, 어부가 사랑에 빠져 거의 먹지도 자지도 못했다는 의미예요.

items.q: "She [was about to] take a sip when the fisherman's face appeared in the tea."에서 [was about to]의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: be about to는 '막 ~하려던 참이다'라는 뜻으로, 차를 막 한 모금 마시려는 순간 어부의 얼굴이 찻물에 나타났다는 의미예요.

items.q: 이 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Wise Old Woman of the Village
A Crystal Heart and a Princess's Tears
How to Make a Teacup from Crystal
items.exp: 어부의 굳어진 마음인 수정이 찻잔이 되어 공주에게 전해지고, 공주가 'her tears fell into the cup'하며 후회하는 이야기예요.

items.q: According to the wise old woman, why did the fisherman's heart turn into a crystal?
choices: The king cast a spell on him.
He had swallowed a crystal by mistake.
He wanted to leave a gift for the princess.
It hardened to block out the pain the princess caused him.
items.exp: 'The princess hurt him so deeply that his heart hardened to block out the pain'이라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

After the princess (A) ___ the fisherman, he died of a broken heart, and his crystal heart, made into a teacup, finally made her feel (B) ___.
items.exp: 공주는 어부를 보고 웃으며 'Shut the door'라고 내쫓았고, 마지막에 'I'm so sorry'라며 후회했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [how cruel she had been]이 가리키는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은? (She remembered how cruel she had been.)
choices: sending the boat down the river
laughing at the fisherman and shutting the door on him
items.exp: 공주는 어부를 보고 'burst out laughing'하고 'Shut the door'라고 명령했는데, 그 잔인했던 행동을 떠올린 거예요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: He took it to the palace, had a teacup [make] from it
the villagers [discovered] him dead in his hut
The princess hurt him so deeply that his heart [hardened]
She remembered how cruel she [had been]
for he [had fallen] deeply in love
items.exp: 사역동사 have의 목적어 a teacup이 '만들어지는' 대상이므로 과거분사 made가 와야 해요. 원문은 'had a teacup made from it'이에요.
